title: Give tips pls (spore x bf2 dogfights)
author: Great_Teacher400
selftext:
A for fun and not profit project to build a multiplayer game with spore and star field fused building mechanics for fully custom ships, boats or tower bases. Used Three.js and want to make water more responsive to the ship. I know I didn't study game sev, I'm from a third world country so sue me for having some fun, but if you can tolerate ai gamedev, please help a brother out. When it's done it'll be a free PvP or pve game on a 1:50 earth that is flooded. Ships go in water, on surface or fly to space(space is a little janky right now), game has some physics breaking addition for testing purposes, like forcing pitch of ship up or down despite g force etc. 

So far using Codex Sol 6.1 light only

Music was copyright free and just placeholder

  
Considering disabling underwater traversal as it has so many bugs when going in or out water. The different physics systems it employs for flight, diving or floating has weird transitions

  
Would love some tips and pointers in the right direction. Inspired by wipeout and battlefield 2 style cat and mouse dog fights from when my brother and I were kids. We'd hunt eachother down for hours

comments.author: Great_Teacher400
comments.body:
I have a cheat shield for landing on water. First person is wip experimental idea. Doesn't lag on my browser but I have an igpu so can't go crazy with Unreal engine etc.
Would love some ideas to make the water better, fun and responsive.

replies.author: FabulusGames
replies.body: Ask Claude or Codex to generate five mock ups of different directions you could take the water, and see if any of them look like something you want to pursue

replies.author: Great_Teacher400
replies.body: I think it's time to ditch codex. It makes a lot of mistakes and often randomly reverses patches to code. Like I removed some UI element and three implements later that changes are somehow reversed. God knows what's happening to the code

replies.author: Great_Teacher400
replies.body:
I'm currently ( as of today) using Gemini to instruct Codex on what to code. Gemini is free in chrome browser and it's much more efficient at explaining why and what to do for water. It seems to be using free GitHub repos for code.
Is that what you mean?

replies.author: FabulusGames
replies.body: No... 1. Stop using Gemini entirely. It's horrible. 2. Ask codex or Claude to explain GitHub to you and get it setup.

comments.author: FabulusGames
comments.body:
I would highly recommend testing out Claude. I have found codex generally only useful for artwork, and fairly infuriating for mostly everything else lately. 

Other than that, I'd have the AI limit test what you can achieve in browser with this type of game with multiplayer. I think your limit is going to be the player's GPU. You may want to consider a particular low-cost animation style that looks good over realism. Just my two cents.

replies.author: Great_Teacher400
replies.body:
I've been hearing a lot that Claude is better suited for this. I'll have to subscribe I guess. 
Low cost animation styles are totally fine by me. Ai wanted to implement full physics for waves and using a vertex to make water move away

replies.author: FabulusGames
replies.body: As a player, I would prefer a smooth unique art style to stuttery realistic water that locks up my PC
